title: Cohort Retention Matrix
description:
Group customers by the month of their **first** order (their cohort). For each cohort month and each later month, report how many of that cohort's customers purchased in that later month — i.e. a retention matrix.

Name the columns `cohort_month`, `month`, and `customers`. A customer is counted in row (cohort C, month M) if they are in cohort C AND made at least one order in month M. Skip rows where `month` equals the cohort month. Return rows ordered by `cohort_month` then `month`.
solutionSql:
WITH firsts AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(strftime('%Y-%m', order_date)) AS cohort_month
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
months AS (
  SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date)
)
SELECT f.cohort_month, m.month, COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM firsts f
JOIN months m ON m.customer_id = f.customer_id
WHERE m.month > f.cohort_month
GROUP BY f.cohort_month, m.month
ORDER BY f.cohort_month, m.month;
hint: Cohort = first-order month. Then join each customer's later purchase months back to their cohort and COUNT per (cohort, month) pair.
outputExplanation: Alice (cohort Jan) and Bob (cohort Jan) both buy in Feb and Mar → 2 for (Jan,Feb) and (Jan,Mar). Carol (cohort Feb) buys in Mar → 1 for (Feb,Mar).

tests.name: No one returns after cohort month
